deviations.observed_behavior: Relational and portable spatial compilation has no qualified catalog SRID proof for Oracle and Db2: ORM INSERT/UPDATE of spatial values and spatial predicates are refused with unsupported before execution, even with declared SRID and an index. Mapping and spatial metadata alone are not enforcement evidence. MariaDB has the same write limit; SQL Server and MariaDB predicates also require catalog proof. Hazard: conforming operations are refused, never silently executed. Reentry: a live-qualified server guard or catalog verification before compilation (spatial_probe::admit_probe).

READ.json and WRITE.json operation documents accept null for optional fields that plan.schema.json types without null (ObjectRef catalog/schema, row_limit, row_offset, filter, srid_policy, spatial parameters) and read it as absent.
The relational IR sends null for absent optional fields (filter without .where(), ObjectRef catalog/schema) and the reader accepts it as absent, although plan.schema.json does not admit null there.
plan::Plan, ReadOperation, WriteOperation and ObjectRef deserialize null as absent in optional fields that plan.schema.json types without null, and serialize absent fields as null.

Query results are limited to 8388608 bytes of compact UTF-8 JSON, before returning any result. The bound is recorded here: capability-attributes-v1 is closed and has no member for it. Hazard: discovery alone cannot reveal the bound. Reentry: adopt a successor attributes contract that declares it.

database.query advertises the catalog JSON and Arrow outputs, but this binding produces only the JSON summary. Hazard: a consumer cannot obtain Arrow from this surface. Reentry: implement an Arrow result path under an explicit versioned selection contract; do not impose a JSON-only restriction on query@1.

The MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and Db2 write adapters accept only plenora.geometry.encoding=wkb and refuse an ewkb geometry field with unsupported while preparing the write, before any effect. CLI, runtime and Python SDK reach the same adapters. Hazard: a conforming EWKB input is refused, never altered. Reentry: a lossless EWKB to WKB conversion qualified by each live gate. PostgreSQL accepts both encodings.

The MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle and Db2 write adapters accept a mixed declaration (any type, or a list) although the target stores only some types, and refuse a value of a type the target cannot store with data_mapping while writing, inside the rolled-back transaction, instead of refusing the field with unsupported before any effect. Hazard: the refusal comes later and as a value class, never as a silent write. Reentry: reject non-storable declared sets while preparing.

Support limits of the write adapters, refused before any effect on conforming input: PostgreSQL refuses with crs, phase prepare, a resolved CRS whose SRID is not in the target spatial_ref_sys (the column would hold SRID 0, a CRS loss); MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and Db2 refuse dimensions they cannot represent or unknown, several declared types and the srid_policy they do not qualify with unsupported; Db2 refuses geography. Reentry: per adapter, by its live gate.

A rejection decided by reading the target (an existing table, spatial_ref_sys, an existing geometry column) is reported with phase prepare, the phase in which database-tools reads the target, not connect or probe. remote_effect is none and retry never, as REJ-003 requires. Hazard: a consumer that keys on the phase label sees prepare. Reentry: map target reads before effect to probe across the adapters.

Read and query outputs assign plenora.field_id from the column origin (PostgreSQL attrelid/attnum) or from the field name (FNV-1a 31 bit), not the smallest unused non-negative integer in field order; an identity registered by a previous write is preserved. Hazard: two components producing the same table assign different ids. Reentry: a contract version that admits stable origin ids, or a positional assignment with a major release.

The MySQL, MariaDB and SQL Server readers declare plenora.geometry.precision=native although those servers store binary64 coordinates, for which GEO-014 requires float64. Hazard: a consumer may assume a grid or decimal coordinate model; the coordinate values are unchanged. Reentry: declare float64 for these adapters, decided by the project owner.

Component bounds on conforming geometry metadata: a negative SRID is refused with unsupported (no adapter represents it), a crs_id longer than 1024 characters or with control characters with crs, a CRS definition over 1 MiB with resource_limit, all before any effect. A schema without plenora.contract.version and without canonical keys is foreign Arrow and is read with the pre-contract legacy keys (plenora.srid, plenora.dimensions, plenora.geometry_type, plenora.spatial_semantics).

Read and query outputs bound the geometry values the database returns (components, nesting, trailing bytes) but do not apply every GEO-011 well-formedness rule to them (ring closure, point counts, member types). Hazard: a value stored invalid by the database is published as is, and a consumer that claims this contract rejects it with data_mapping; nothing is altered. Reentry: apply plenora_database_core::geometry_value to read outputs once each live gate qualifies it.

A geometry field whose crs_id is EPSG:<n> and whose plenora.geometry.srid is a different integer is refused with crs before any effect, on every Arrow ingress: database-tools writes the SRID as the CRS of the column and does not choose between two identities. Hazard: a conforming input that pairs a registry identifier with a different local SRID is refused, never written with either. Reentry: a contract rule on the relation between srid and crs_id.

Every write adapter stores the first WKB ordinate as x (longitude or easting); MySQL exchanges WKB with axis-order=long-lat (write, read, query, relational mutations, SDK) and reads x/y after ST_SRID(g,0). A lat_lon or northing_easting field is refused with unsupported before any effect, never swapped; unknown and other are written as stored. Hazard: an unknown or other field stored north-first lands swapped. Reentry: a contract version that refuses unknown.

An SRID derived from crs_id EPSG:<n> without plenora.geometry.srid is written only after the target catalog registers n as EPSG:n (PostgreSQL spatial_ref_sys, MySQL ST_SPATIAL_REFERENCE_SYSTEMS), otherwise crs before any effect. MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and Db2 do not derive and refuse with crs: no catalog, local ids, or a lookup not qualified live. Hazard: a conforming input is refused, never mislabelled. Reentry: a live qualified catalog lookup per adapter.

PostgreSQL write refuses before any effect, deciding from the schema: a LargeBinary geoarrow.wkb field (unsupported; the codecs read Binary), a geography field without SRID (crs; PostGIS would assign 4326) or with a projected axis order (unsupported); reading spatial_ref_sys, a geography SRID that is not geographic (unsupported). Reentry: LargeBinary codecs qualified by the live gate.

PostgreSQL read and query publish a geometry column without SRID in the catalog (no typmod, or a computed geometry not inheriting a column SRID through preserving functions) with crs_resolution missing, and refuse with crs, phase read, a value that carries an SRID; a declared or inherited SRID must be on every value. Hazard: such columns, mixed-SRID tables included, need a typmod or a cast. Reentry: a contract version that admits per-value SRIDs.

A plenora.field_id registered in a PostgreSQL column comment by earlier versions with leading zeros (00<n>) is read and published in canonical form (<n>); new input with leading zeros stays a schema defect, and new registrations are canonical. Hazard: the published id text differs from the registered one, the identity is the same. Reentry: no comment registered by earlier versions remains.
